symptoms: Olive-green to dark brown or black velvety spots on leaves
Deformed, puckered, or curling leaves
Yellowing of leaf tissue surrounding lesions
Premature leaf drop in severe infections
Corky, scabby brown lesions on fruit
treatment: Apply protective fungicides (Captan, Mancozeb, or copper-based sprays) in early spring before rain.
Prune overcrowded branches to improve air circulation and sunlight penetration.
Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn to eliminate overwintering fungal spores.
Avoid overhead watering; use drip irrigation to keep foliage dry.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Plant scab-resistant cultivars such as Liberty, Enterprise, or Freedom, and maintain regular orchard sanitation.

symptoms: Small purple spots on upper leaf surfaces expanding into 'frogeye' spots with tan centers and purple margins
Black sunken cankers on twigs and tree bark
Firm brown decay on fruit turning completely black with mummified texture
treatment: Prune out dead wood, cankers, and blighted twigs during the dormant season.
Apply thiophanate-methyl, captan, or sulfur sprays starting at petal fall.
Remove and burn all mummified apples remaining on branches or the ground.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Sterilize pruning tools between cuts using 70% isopropyl alcohol or 10% bleach solution, and avoid mechanical injury to tree trunks.

symptoms: Bright yellow-orange or reddish spots on upper leaf surfaces
Tiny black raised dots (pycnia) inside orange lesions
Fringe-like fungal tube structures (aecia) on the underside of leaves
Premature defoliation and stunted tree vigor
treatment: Apply preventive fungicides containing myclobutanil or mancozeb at pink bud stage through early summer.
Remove nearby Eastern red cedar or juniper trees that serve as alternate hosts within a 1-2 mile radius if practical.
Prune out rust galls from nearby juniper bushes before spring rains.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Select resistant apple varieties such as Dayton, Redfree, or William's Pride.

symptoms: Uniform vibrant green coloration
Smooth leaf margins without spots, wilting, or curling
Firm leaf turgor and normal vegetative development
treatment: No chemical or corrective treatment needed.
Maintain consistent seasonal irrigation and balanced fertilization (N-P-K).
Apple___healthy.prevention: Continue periodic scouting for early signs of pests or mildew and ensure good soil drainage.

symptoms: Small, powdery cinnamon-brown to dark orange pustules on both upper and lower leaf surfaces
Pustules rupture epidermal tissue, releasing powdery spores
Leaves turn yellow and may wither prematurely under high humidity
treatment: Apply foliar fungicides (strobilurins or triazoles) if pustules appear before tassel emergence and weather is cool and moist.
Ensure balanced soil potassium levels to support leaf cell wall resistance.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention: Plant rust-resistant hybrid corn seeds; rotate crops with non-grass crops like legumes.

symptoms: Long, elliptical, cigar-shaped grayish-green to tan lesions (1-6 inches long)
Lesions coalesce, causing large areas of leaf necrosis
Premature death of leaves giving fields a burned or frost-damaged appearance
treatment: Apply dual-mode foliar fungicides (QoI + DMI) at early silk emergence.
Incorporate deep tillage of crop debris after harvest to bury fungal inoculants.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Choose corn hybrids containing Ht-resistance genes and practice a 2-year crop rotation.

symptoms: Long, arching, vibrant green foliage
Clear, prominent central veins without discoloration or pustules
Robust stalk attachment and vigorous photosynthesis
treatment: No treatment required.
Maintain nitrogen sidedressing during active vegetative growth.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.prevention: Maintain soil moisture during pollination and continue standard weed and pest management.

symptoms: Dark brown to black lesions showing distinctive concentric rings ('target board' pattern)
Lesions initially develop on older, lower foliage and progress upward
Chlorotic yellow halos surrounding necrotic spots
Severe defoliation leading to reduced tuber sizing
treatment: Apply chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or azoxystrobin at early symptom onset.
Remove and destroy severely affected lower leaves to reduce spore spread.
Avoid excessive overhead sprinkling in late afternoon to reduce leaf wetness hours.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Practice a 3-4 year crop rotation away from solanaceous plants; maintain optimal plant nutrition to prevent plant stress.

symptoms: Water-soaked dark green to purplish-black irregular lesions on leaves
White fuzzy mildew growth on leaf undersides during cool, humid mornings
Rapidly collapsing and rotting stems with foul odor
Tuber infection leading to dry granular reddish-brown rot
treatment: Immediately apply systemic fungicides containing metalaxyl, cymoxanil, or dimethomorph.
Destroy and bag heavily infested plants immediately; do NOT compost them.
Stop overhead irrigation immediately to minimize leaf moisture.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Plant certified disease-free seed tubers, eliminate cull piles, and monitor local late blight weather warning alerts.

symptoms: Broad, compound dark green leaflets
Supple texture with even leaf margins
No spotting, necrosis, or edge burning
treatment: No treatment required.
Keep soil evenly moist, especially during tuber initiation and bulking.
Potato___healthy.prevention: Hilling soil over developing tubers to prevent greening and fungal contamination.

symptoms: Small (less than 3mm), dark brown, water-soaked circular spots with yellow halos
Leaf spots may look greasy and dry to form ragged holes
Extensive leaf yellowing, browning, and premature drop
Raised black blister-like scabs on tomato fruits
treatment: Spray copper-based bactericides combined with mancozeb for improved bacterial suppression.
Avoid handling or working among wet plants to prevent spreading bacteria across foliage.
Sanitize all stakes, cages, and pruning shears thoroughly.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified pathogen-free seeds, hot-water treat seeds before planting, and use drip irrigation at base of plants.

symptoms: Brown to black circular spots with concentric target-like rings
Starts on oldest leaves closest to the ground and works upward
Surrounding leaf tissue turns yellow and eventually wilts and falls off
Dark sunken lesions on stems and fruit calyx
treatment: Prune off the lowest 12-18 inches of leaves once plants are established to prevent soil splash.
Apply bio-fungicides (Bacillus subtilis) or copper/chlorothalonil sprays at first sign.
Mulch heavily around the plant base with clean straw or plastic mulch.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Rotate crops every 3 years away from tomatoes, peppers, and eggplants; stake plants for proper air movement.

symptoms: Large, irregularly shaped pale to greasy dark-brown lesions
White fungal fuzzy growth on underside of leaves in humid weather
Greasy dark brown patches on green or ripening tomatoes
Whole plant can turn brown, shrivel, and collapse within 7 to 14 days
treatment: Promptly apply protective or systemic fungicides (copper, chlorothalonil, or mandipropamid).
Severely affected plants should be removed, sealed in bags, and discarded in trash.
Keep plant canopies dry by providing ample spacing and avoiding evening watering.
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Plant resistant tomato cultivars (e.g., Defiant, Mountain Merit, Iron Lady) and scout garden twice weekly.

symptoms: Pale green to yellow diffuse spots on upper leaf surfaces
Olive-green to velvety brown mold growth on corresponding undersides of leaves
Affected leaves curl, wither, and drop prematurely
Most prevalent in high humidity greenhouse and high-tunnel environments
treatment: Increase ventilation, exhaust fans, and heating in greenhouses to reduce relative humidity below 85%.
Apply potassium bicarbonate, neem oil, or sulfur-based fungicides.
Remove affected lower leaves to lower spore count.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Select leaf mold resistant hybrid varieties and space plants generously for cross ventilation.

symptoms: Lush, deep green serrated compound foliage
Stout hairy stems with no discoloration or wilting
Active flowering and robust fruit set
treatment: No corrective treatment required.
Feed with balanced tomato fertilizer rich in calcium to prevent blossom end rot.
Tomato___healthy.prevention: Maintain consistent deep watering and apply organic mulch around root zones.
